scope: Research-only audit of avionics, electrical fault protection, timekeeping, and assurance. Recommendations concern the educational application's representative hardware and named civil examples. They do not establish any military implementation.
applicationDecision: Add finer computer anatomy under the existing computer parent, not another major scene. The strongest additions are recovery memory, memory-protection logic, and reset circuitry. Explain spacecraft time and safing as functions. Most power protection, redundancy-management, and telemetry assemblies are already present.

priorityMeaning.P1: Important educational omission to address in a future product revision; not a claim that this hardware is mandatory on every satellite.
priorityMeaning.P2: Useful optional comparison or refinement after the main omissions are addressed.
priorityMeaning.covered: Present in the current catalog; improve explanation or diagram rather than create a duplicate.
priorityMeaning.defer: Not admitted as new evidence in this audit.

candidateAdditions.name: Boot and recovery memory
candidateAdditions.existingCoverage: comp-command-data-memory explains sequence/data storage, but not a protected startup or recovery image.
candidateAdditions.recommendation: Split recovery storage from working/data memory in a representative computer-board inset. Label the implementation illustrative; do not assign a capacity or part number.
row: Permanent memory can retain processor boot/safe-hold code or a basic programmable-logic configuration

candidateAdditions.name: Memory interface and error-correction logic
candidateAdditions.kind: physical circuitry and associated maintenance function
candidateAdditions.existingCoverage: Generic memory is present; no EDAC/ECC explanation appears in the inspected catalog.
candidateAdditions.recommendation: Add a board-level callout beside memory. Present scrubbing as an associated operation, not a second unexplained hardware box. Do not promise correction of every fault.
row: Memory interfaces implement error detection and correction appropriate to their application
supportingRow: ECC, watchdogs, scrubbing, and redundancy are complementary mitigation approaches

candidateAdditions.name: Power-on-reset circuitry
candidateAdditions.existingCoverage: RMC reboot is covered, but board startup/reset sequencing is not.
candidateAdditions.recommendation: Add a small supporting callout tied to the power and computer diagram; avoid inventing a standalone supervisor box or exact circuit.
row: Reset circuitry coordinates startup and protects critical signals while power and clocks settle

candidateAdditions.name: Spacecraft time counter
candidateAdditions.kind: functional element; no separate physical clock package inferred
candidateAdditions.existingCoverage: ABI Telemetry and Timing card and RF reference oscillator are present. The spacecraft time-tagging role is not explicitly distinguished.
candidateAdditions.recommendation: Add a time-tag path to the data diagram and a computer detail entry. Keep spacecraft time, detector timing, and radio frequency reference distinct.
row: A data-system counter schedules activity and time-tags engineering and science data

refs: Spacecraft Clock, first and third paragraphs

candidateAdditions.name: Latching current limiter
candidateAdditions.existingCoverage: GOES-R PDMs, current sensing, and fuse boards already explain distribution and overcurrent protection.
candidateAdditions.recommendation: Optional comparison in Parts or Glossary. Do not place an LCL into the GOES-R model without mission evidence or describe it as mandatory.
row: Switchable protection between source and load limits overcurrent and then latches off

bestPracticeExplanations.name: Fault protection and safe operating states
bestPracticeExplanations.recommendation: Add a concise normal/recovery/safe-state diagram connecting existing power, attitude, thermal, and communications hardware. This is explanatory content, not an extra component or military operational sequence.
row: Preserve spacecraft resources and commandability while maintaining a sustainable power and thermal state

bestPracticeExplanations.name: Fault containment and redundancy boundaries
bestPracticeExplanations.recommendation: Explain why extra boxes alone do not establish resilience. Draw a selected alternate path only when its named civil source verifies it.
row: Redundancy depends on containing faults within defined regions

bestPracticeExplanations.name: Radiation hardness assurance
bestPracticeExplanations.recommendation: Add a Method note explaining the evidence needed before calling hardware radiation-qualified. No generic shield thickness, dose rating, or universal radiation-proof label belongs on the teaching model.
row: Project-specific assurance addresses ionizing dose, displacement damage, and single-event effects in EEE components

coveredOrDoNotAdd.name: Independent watchdog or recovery supervisor box
coveredOrDoNotAdd.reason: The catalog already names GOES-R's Redundancy Management Card and its heartbeat/reboot role. Explain it more clearly rather than add a duplicate generic assembly.
row: Recovery can use external reset resources; independence of clock and reset resources matters

coveredOrDoNotAdd.name: Power-distribution and health-monitoring assemblies
coveredOrDoNotAdd.reason: These are already named in the catalog. Visibility and diagram connections are the likely remaining product issue.

coveredOrDoNotAdd.name: Universal redundant computer count or triple-modular voter
coveredOrDoNotAdd.decision: do not add as a universal component
coveredOrDoNotAdd.reason: Named civil redundancy examples are already available. A new fixed count or voting topology would require specific evidence and is unnecessary for the application.
row: Architecture and redundancy choices depend on mission requirements and accepted risk

refs: Section 8.1, paragraphs on large and small spacecraft architecture

coveredOrDoNotAdd.name: Safing box, radiation-hardness box, or standalone memory-scrubbing box
coveredOrDoNotAdd.reason: These labels confuse functions or assurance practices with physical components. Tie the explanations to actual computer, memory, power, and interface hardware.

coveredOrDoNotAdd.name: Specific processor model, science-recorder capacity, radiation dose rating, or redundant hardware count
coveredOrDoNotAdd.reason: The reviewed guidance does not establish those properties for the representative satellite. Product-table figures are intentionally excluded.
